Look folks, we are watching the steady decay of basic law and order right before our eyes, all thanks to progressive judicial thinking that cares more about coddling criminals than protecting law-abiding families and their homes. 

Just look at the Punjab and Haryana High Court, where Justice Sumeet Goel has handed down a ruling that essentially rolls out the red carpet for criminals in house trespass and theft-related matters. According to this decision, anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Instead, they are demanding "clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances." 

This is an absolute betrayal of public safety and family security. When the courts dismiss a plea seeking the cancellation of pre-arrest bail just because the stolen goods haven't been recovered, it sends all the wrong signals to lawbreakers. This is what happens when procedural loopholes are prioritized over the authority of the law and the protection of innocent victims left waiting for justice. We desperately need an unwavering commitment to strict accountability, tradition, and order—not activist judges making it easier for suspects to stay out of custody while victims suffer.
